ENGLISH — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. going

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

4. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

6. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

7. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. blue
   C. run
   D. happiness

8. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

12. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

13. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

15. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Conjunctions – because, that, when, if, unles and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative Composition 10.5.1 Packing and Shopping lists 11.5.1 Spelling Antonyms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Oral Presentations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Presentations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
